articles.title: Mapping Memory: Reconstructing Architecture Beyond Physical Evidence
articles.summary: How do you remember the dimensions of a room you could barely see? Perhaps through the distance between footsteps, the sound of a door closing, or the way an echo travels down a corridor . For someone who has been denied the ability to see or move freely through a space, these fragments may be the only record of its architecture.

articles.title: Pod for Happiness / Craft Narrative
articles.summary: In the small village of Hignigada near Baramati , Maharashtra, a young village head approached us to build an outdoor play area for school children. The school campus had a large playground divided by an avenue of seven trees, with classrooms arranged along the perimeter. Villagers fondly shared how they enjoyed evening walks and sitting under the trees. Inspired by this connection to nature & community space, we designed the play area around the banyan tree, making it the centerpiece of the insert.

articles.title: Large Glass Openings at Work in a Production Facility
articles.summary: Integrating truck access into a glazed facade requires coordinating panel dimensions, opening mechanisms, and the space needed for vehicles to maneuver. These decisions affect both the composition of the facade and how materials and products move in and out of the building. Glass thus becomes part of the daily workflow: when closed, it encloses the space and admits natural light; when open, it allows loading and unloading to take place.

articles.title: A two-way facade / CYS.ASDO
articles.summary: The façade addresses two simultaneous relationships: how the city sees the building, and how occupants see the city. Openings in the outer façade and interior enclosure respond to the spaces they serve. Some align to extend views outward; others are offset to redirect sightlines. Walls, terraces, and planting filter the surroundings into selected views.

articles.title: Dream House / Seiro Arquitectos
